learning_outcomes: Choose between RAG, long-context (+ caching), fine-tuning, and tool-use for a given workload, and justify the decision using freshness, privacy, cost, latency, and traceability constraints.
Implement a minimal indexing pipeline (load → chunk → embed → store) with stable document IDs, metadata, and a reproducible re-indexing strategy.
Configure hybrid retrieval (BM25 + dense) and demonstrate a measurable improvement in Recall@K on a small evaluation set.
Add a precision layer (reranker or late-interaction retriever) and measure improvements in Context Precision and/or nDCG compared to baseline retrieval.
Apply contextual retrieval and late chunking, run an ablation, and explain when each helps or hurts retrieval quality.
Design an evaluation harness that scores Recall@K, Context Precision, Answer Faithfulness, and Answer Relevance, and define production gates for regression prevention.
Implement a corrective/agentic RAG loop that blocks generation when evidence is weak, triggers re-retrieval, and reduces unsupported claims in evaluation logs.
Explain GraphRAG and RAPTOR-style hierarchical retrieval and identify when they outperform flat chunk retrieval (and when they add unnecessary complexity).

key_facts.fact: ColBERTv2-style late-interaction retrieval (token-level MaxSim) is still a practical high-precision option; verify its 2024–2025 benchmark position and the best-maintained open-source implementations before presenting it as a recommended approach.
verification_notes: Confirm accuracy/latency tradeoffs vs modern dense retrievers on BEIR/MTEB-style tasks.
Confirm how ColBERT-style indices scale (storage, latency) and what hardware assumptions are reasonable in 2025.

key_facts.fact: ‘Late chunking’ (token-level embedding first, then pooling into chunk representations) can reduce boundary breakage vs naive chunking; verify the current best-practice algorithm and library support (and whether it is still called ‘late chunking’) before teaching it as a default.
verification_notes: Find at least one credible technical write-up or paper and cross-check that the lesson’s description matches it.
Validate where it helps (long docs, table-heavy docs) and where it may not (short FAQ chunks).

key_facts.fact: Anthropic popularized ‘contextual retrieval’ (adding a short context summary to each chunk before embedding); verify Anthropic’s exact recommended procedure, reported gains, and any updated guidance in 2024–2025 docs/blog posts.
verification_notes: Confirm whether the recommended summary length, placement, and metadata strategy changed since initial publication.
Verify any quantitative claims (benchmark/task) before including them as numbers.

key_facts.fact: GraphRAG approaches (graph construction + retrieval over graph structure) evolved rapidly; verify the latest Microsoft/academic ‘GraphRAG’ implementations, recommended graph-building pipelines, and evaluation results before positioning it as ‘the’ modern approach.
verification_notes: Confirm open-source project names/repos and whether they are actively maintained.
Verify when GraphRAG is worth it (multi-hop/global questions) vs when it is overkill (simple policy Q&A).

key_facts.fact: RAPTOR-style hierarchical retrieval (recursive summarization + tree search) has multiple variants; verify the current canonical paper(s), reproducible baselines, and whether ‘RAPTOR’ is still a recommended default in 2025 tooling.
verification_notes: Confirm how modern RAG frameworks (e.g., LlamaIndex/LangChain) implement hierarchical retrieval and what parameters matter.
Verify failure modes (summary drift, information loss) and how to mitigate them.

key_facts.fact: LanceDB became a common modern choice for local/embedded vector search; verify its current (2025) support for hybrid search, filtering, index types, and production-readiness claims before recommending it.
verification_notes: Confirm current docs for hybrid search and the expected deployment footprint.
Verify the recommended index types and performance guidance for 2025.

key_facts.fact: Milvus 2.x introduced/expanded hybrid retrieval features; verify the exact Milvus 2.x version and supported hybrid/BM25 workflows in 2025 before adding it to the ‘vector DB selection’ section.
verification_notes: Confirm how Milvus recommends doing hybrid retrieval and whether BM25 is built-in or via an integration.
Confirm operational guidance (index build time, replication, resource needs).

key_facts.fact: ‘RAG vs long context’ guidance depends on real model context limits; verify the current maximum context windows and pricing/latency tradeoffs for models that advertise very large contexts (e.g., ~200k to ~2M tokens) before using numbers in the decision matrix.
verification_notes: Confirm which models actually support the advertised context (and under what plan/endpoint).
Verify that ‘lost-in-the-middle’ and chunk ordering issues still apply at these context sizes.

key_facts.fact: Even with very long contexts, models can under-attend to mid-context evidence (‘lost in the middle’); verify current best practices (chunk ordering, compression, citation prompting) and whether vendors provide mitigations as of 2025.
verification_notes: Confirm current vendor guidance on long-context retrieval/compression and any context-caching features.
Validate with at least one recent reproduction or vendor/academic write-up.

key_facts.fact: RAG evaluation tooling (Ragas/TruLens/DeepEval or equivalents) changed quickly; verify the current recommended metrics, defaults, and integration patterns in 2025 before baking them into labs or screenshots.
verification_notes: Confirm which framework is actively maintained and best fits the course stack.
Verify metric definitions (faithfulness/groundedness) and known pitfalls of LLM-as-judge.

key_facts.fact: Popular reranking models (hosted APIs and open models) evolve and licensing changes; verify the current recommended rerankers for production (and their licensing) before listing specific model names in 2025 content.
verification_notes: Confirm performance vs latency tradeoffs and what is feasible on CPU-only deployments.
Confirm whether a given reranker is suitable for multilingual (EN/CS) corpora.

key_facts.fact: Production RAG must enforce document-level permissions (ACLs) at retrieval time to prevent data leakage; verify best-practice patterns (pre-filtering, post-filtering, per-tenant indexes) and include at least one explicit warning section.
verification_notes: Confirm how common vector DBs implement metadata filters and what is safe vs foot-gun.
Add ‘what can go wrong’ examples (cross-tenant leakage) without including sensitive details.

categories.name: Hook
checks: Hook lands in the first 30 seconds (bold claim or provocative question).
Motivates RAG with a concrete failure story (hallucination/knowledge cutoff/private data).
Sets a clear mission for the learner and previews the payoff.
Includes at least one memorable line, analogy, or mini-demo prompt.

categories.name: Structure
checks: Progression is clear: indexing → retrieval → reranking → generation → evaluation → agentic loop.
Key terms are defined once and reused consistently (chunk, recall@K, groundedness).
Decision points are explicit (when to use RAG vs long context vs fine-tune).
Ends with a Holocron summary and actionable checklist.

categories.name: Labs
checks: Labs are ‘missions’ with copy/paste prompts or code, expected outputs, and time-box guidance.
At least one lab teaches debugging a retrieval failure (not just ‘happy path’).
At least one lab introduces evaluation/metrics and shows how to detect regressions.
Labs align to outcomes and escalate difficulty without big jumps.

categories.name: Visuals
checks: Visual anchor every 3–5 paragraphs (diagrams, tables, concept cards).
Diagrams are readable on mobile (no tiny text, no overlap).
Complex concepts have at least one explanatory diagram (hybrid search, agentic loop, eval triad).
Any UI-specific step includes a real screenshot (if applicable).

categories.name: Accuracy
checks: Claims about ‘2024–2025’ techniques are either cited or marked as ‘verify’ with a source plan.
No outdated or misleading model/product references in ‘current’ recommendations.
Distinguishes recall vs precision vs faithfulness (and does not conflate them).
Explains limitations honestly (RAG reduces hallucinations; does not guarantee truth).

categories.name: Engagement
checks: Uses story beats, tension (failure modes), and ‘aha moments’ to sustain attention.
Includes at least 2 interactive moments (quick question, prediction, or mini self-check).
Keeps energy high with callouts, bold formatting, and concrete examples.
Avoids long, unbroken exposition blocks; balances text, visuals, and labs.

required_knowledge: Familiarity with embeddings and vector similarity

must_be_true_facts.fact: RAG conditions generation on retrieved external documents at query time, allowing new information to be injected without retraining.

sources.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks

must_be_true_facts.fact: Hybrid retrieval combines sparse keyword matching (BM25) with dense vector similarity to improve recall for exact terms and semantic matches.

sources.title: The Probabilistic Relevance Framework: BM25 and Beyond
sources.citation: Robertson, S., & Zaragoza, H. (2009). Foundations and Trends in IR.

must_be_true_facts.fact: Neural rerankers (e.g., BERT cross-encoders) can substantially improve precision by jointly encoding query+passage, after an initial high-recall retrieval stage.
Language models can perform worse when relevant evidence is placed in the middle of long contexts (‘lost in the middle’), motivating chunk ordering and compression strategies.

sources.title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts

dont_claim: Don’t claim RAG eliminates hallucinations; it only reduces them when retrieval is correct and grounding rules are enforced.
Don’t present dense vector search as sufficient for exact-match terms; hybrid search is often required for IDs, acronyms, and regulatory language.
Don’t imply long-context models make retrieval obsolete; selection, ordering, and faithfulness checks still matter (and ‘lost in the middle’ remains a risk).
Don’t include time-sensitive model names, context limits, or pricing without verifying from vendor docs as of 2025.
Don’t promise citations are always correct without verification; retrieved sources can be irrelevant, outdated, or incorrect.
